assumptions: Target merchants use multiple PSPs or commerce systems and therefore experience evidence fragmentation not solved by one native tool.
Merchants can lawfully grant scoped access and approve each high-risk submission before it is sent.
The service avoids unnecessary card-data scope and can meet merchant security and GDPR requirements.
No recovery improvement, paid customer, privileged dataset, or platform distribution agreement has yet been demonstrated.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid multi-PSP pilots showing eligible dispute volume, reliable evidence ingestion and submission, lower handling time, statistically credible incremental net recovery after fees, acceptable security review, and repeatable customer acquisition.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A merchant-authorized checkpoint that joins evidence across payment providers, storefronts, fulfillment, refunds, and communications addresses fragmentation that any single PSP sees only partially, though dispute automation is an established category.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A dispute immediately reverses revenue, adds fees, consumes staff time, and imposes a deadline, creating an observable loss and a clear budget owner; incremental willingness to pay beyond native PSP tooling is not yet evidenced.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-case, subscription, and recovery-linked pricing align revenue with a measurable event and require modest capital, but integration maintenance, security, human review, collection timing, and heterogeneous cases leave contribution margin and CAC payback hypothetical.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: EU merchants using multiple PSPs form a coherent beachhead with repeated cases, but reachable merchant count, recoverable case volume, vertical concentration, and dissatisfaction with native tools are unquantified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Cross-PSP portability is useful, but PSPs already provide guided or automated evidence and specialized dispute-management vendors can pursue the same merchants; the venture lacks an exclusive channel or workflow position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted payment-evidence layer could expand across PSPs, storefronts, vertical templates, prevention, refund operations, and other transaction exceptions once merchant integrations are established.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned outcome labels can improve packet prioritization, but access is revocable, integrations are nonexclusive, network rules change, and the merchant or PSP retains the underlying data and decision interface.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The cross-system evidence join, human approval gate, and outcome tracking offer a concrete advantage for multi-PSP merchants, and the work fits the founder's classification and document-extraction skills.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Continued e-commerce volume and better document automation help adoption, but PSP automation is advancing simultaneously and no specific regulatory or platform change creates a protected entry window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Performance-tracked pilots, agencies, fractional CFOs, accountants, and permitted app ecosystems are plausible channels, but no channel access, conversion rate, or acquisition cost has been validated.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A manual-first product is feasible within the capital and time constraints, but privacy, security, PSP terms, changing network rules, and the risk of consuming a merchant's only evidence round demand strong controls.

highest_value_structural_change: Concentrate on one evidence-heavy merchant vertical using at least two PSPs, require merchant approval, and price against measured net incremental recovery and handling-time reduction versus each PSP's native workflow.
main_structural_strength: The paid event, loss, deadline, responsible buyer, and outcome are directly measurable, enabling a low-capital, feedback-rich service workflow.
primary_score_limiter: Native PSP automation and existing dispute vendors compress differentiation, while cross-platform API coverage and incremental recovery remain unproven.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Stripe already offers guided and automated evidence tooling, and the issuer rather than the evidence provider controls the final outcome.
